newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower, supply concerns loom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower, supply concerns loom.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished slightly lower, as supply concerns loomed over the market despite data confirming a slowdown in U.S. economic activity, traders and analysts said.
U.S. Treasury will sell $10.0 billion 10-year notes Wednesday and auction $10.0 billion 30-year T-bonds Thursday.
Treasury will begin auctioning Tuesday with the sale of $18.5 billion three-year notes.
"It's really amazing the Treasury will be auctioning three-years (notes) on election day," one floor trader said.
One major fund alone sold 4,000 March contracts.
"They want to be squared away as much as possible ahead of the elections," one trader said.

He also noted that funds and money managers were still pushing money into the intermediate part of the curve, and selling the front four Eurodollar futures contracts against five- to seven-year notes.
He said that after the Sept 24 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, most dealers and funds increased activity in the two-year note sector from Eurodollars.
